quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You see a green traffic light ahead, but cars are blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you cannot enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street, you must:

options.text: Always yield the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross.
Yield only if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog signals a blind or partially blind pedestrian. You must always yield to them, regardless of where they are crossing.

questions.question: If a traffic signal is broken and not working, you must:

options.text: Stop, then go when it is safe.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic signal like a four-way stop. Stop at the intersection, check that it is safe, then proceed carefully.

questions.question: You see animals near the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Animals can suddenly move onto the road or change direction. They often travel in groups, so more animals may be nearby out of sight. Slow down and be cautious.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Drive through carefully and do not stare at the workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully and do not stare at the workers.
questions.explanation: Do not stare or slow down to look at unusual things. This causes traffic congestion. Drive through the construction zone at a safe speed.

questions.question: You are driving in the far right lane of a four-lane freeway. You notice thick broken white lines on the left side of your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You are in a carpool lane and must move to another lane.
You are in a lane for slow-moving vehicles.
You are in an exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in an exit lane.
questions.explanation: Large broken lines on the pavement mark lanes that are ending. Be ready to exit the freeway or for the lane to merge.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes to green.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction when the road is clear, even if the main light is red. You must be in the lane marked for that arrow.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows that the road splits. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers. Make sure no vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: High beams reflect off fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Always use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist. Fog lights can also help if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: When a cyclist is making a left turn:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Cyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see cyclists in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the side rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show blind spots by definition. You must turn and look over your shoulders to check these areas.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive closer than you would to a car.
Drive farther back than you would to a car.
Stay to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would to a car.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have bigger blind spots. You need more distance to stop safely and to see around the truck.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is starting.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is starting.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a divided highway is beginning. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent skidding. Keep your tires in good condition. If you start to skid, ease off the gas, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. Always check that you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes and you have plenty of room.

questions.question: When can you drive a vehicle in a bike lane?

options.text: If you drive slower than 15 mph.
No more than 200 feet before turning right.
Whenever there are no cyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 200 feet before turning right.
questions.explanation: You may enter a bike lane only within 200 feet of a right turn. Do not enter a bike lane at any other time.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Only affect large vehicles.
Only reduce visibility.
Can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can be a problem for all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility and can physically push any vehicle off course.

questions.question: Your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.
questions.explanation: At speeds as low as 30 mph in heavy rain, your tires may lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: Before you turn on the ignition, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Develop a routine for getting in and out of your car. Before turning on the ignition, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and only proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect driving ability if taken as directed.
Medications are always safe to take if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous and affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and impair your ability to drive. You are responsible for knowing how your medications affect your driving.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first and then stop.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a comfortable ride. If your vehicle bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert and proceed carefully. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: You are driving on a freeway with a 65 mph speed limit. Traffic is moving at 70 mph. You may legally drive:

options.text: 70 mph or faster to keep up with traffic.
Between 65 mph and 70 mph.
No faster than 65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: No faster than 65 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit is 65 mph on most highways. You can only drive 70 mph if the speed limit sign shows 70 mph.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road in front of the car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around the vehicle. You need to know what is happening beside, ahead, and behind your car at all times.

questions.question: When weather or light requires you to use your lights while driving:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your high beams.
Use your low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Increase as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe at higher speeds.

questions.question: To make a right turn at a corner, you:

options.text: May not enter the bicycle lane.
Should only enter the bicycle lane if you stop before turning.
Must enter the bicycle lane before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must enter the bicycle lane before turning.
questions.explanation: When making a right turn where there is a bicycle lane, you must enter it no more than 200 feet before the corner. Make sure no bicyclists are in your way before you move into the lane.

questions.question: Animals can be transported in the back of a pickup truck only if:

options.text: The sides of the truck bed are at least 18 inches high.
They are properly secured.
The tailgate of the truck is closed.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are properly secured.
questions.explanation: Animals must be properly secured in the back of a truck to prevent them from falling, jumping, or being thrown from the vehicle.

questions.question: To avoid sudden moves, you should look ahead to where your vehicle will be in about:

options.text: 5 to 10 seconds.
10 to 15 seconds.
15 to 20 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds.
questions.explanation: Scan the road 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This gives you time to see hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: When entering a work zone, signs will warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.
